title: Qin Et Al.-2025-Large Language Models
chunk_summaries: The research article titled "Large Language Models Meet NLP: A Survey," published in Frontiers in Computer Science in 2025, provides a comprehensive overview of the intersection between large language models (LLMs) and natural language processing (NLP). The authors, Libo Qin, Qiguang Chen, Xiachong Feng, Yang Wu, Yongheng Zhang, Yinghui Li, Min Li, Wanxiang Che, and Philip S. Yu, represent various institutions including Central South University, Harbin Institute of Technology, the University of Hong Kong, Tsinghua University, and the University of Illinois at Chicago. The article spans pages 1 to 35 and is accessible via the provided DOI link.

This study investigates the application of large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, in Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks, addressing key questions about their current use, the resolution of traditional NLP tasks, and future prospects. It introduces a unified taxonomy categorizing LLMs into two paradigms: parameter-frozen and parameter-tuning, providing a comprehensive overview of their progress in NLP. The research also highlights new frontiers and challenges in the field, aiming to inspire further advancements and offering insights into the potential and limitations of LLMs, while serving as a practical guide for developing effective LLMs in NLP.

This paper presents a comprehensive survey of Large Language Models (LLMs) and their applications in Natural Language Processing (NLP), highlighting significant advancements such as impressive zero-shot performance and emergent abilities like instruction following and in-context learning. It categorizes LLM applications into two paradigms: parameter-frozen (including zero-shot and few-shot learning) and parameter-tuning (including full-parameter and parameter-efficient tuning). The study aims to address key questions regarding the current use of LLMs in NLP tasks, their effectiveness compared to traditional models, and future research directions. Additionally, it introduces a new taxonomy for understanding LLMs in NLP, discusses emerging research areas and challenges, and provides a curated collection of LLM resources for researchers. The authors hope this work will inspire further advancements in LLM-based NLP.

The text outlines two paradigms for adapting large language models (LLMs) for natural language processing (NLP) tasks: the parameter-frozen paradigm and the parameter-tuning paradigm. The parameter-frozen paradigm includes zero-shot learning, where LLMs solve tasks based on instruction prompts without tuning, and few-shot learning, which uses in-context demonstrations for task completion. In contrast, the parameter-tuning paradigm involves adjusting LLM parameters, encompassing full-parameter tuning, where all model parameters are fine-tuned, and parameter-efficient tuning (PET), which modifies a subset of parameters for specific tasks. A comparison of these paradigms reveals that zero-shot learning is the most resource-efficient with strong out-of-domain generalization, while full-parameter tuning offers the best in-domain performance but is the least efficient. Few-shot learning provides better in-domain results than zero-shot but requires more resources, and parameter-efficient tuning balances performance and efficiency, sometimes surpassing full-parameter tuning under limited resources.

The text outlines various Natural Language Processing (NLP) understanding tasks, including Semantic Analysis, Information Extraction, Dialogue Understanding, and Table Understanding. It discusses sentiment analysis as a key NLP function, detailing two paradigms: Parameter-Frozen and Parameter-Tuning. In sentiment analysis, zero-shot and few-shot learning techniques enhance performance, while full-parameter and parameter-efficient tuning approaches optimize models for specific tasks. Information Extraction focuses on extracting structured data from text, employing similar learning paradigms to improve accuracy and efficiency. Dialogue Understanding encompasses spoken language understanding and dialogue state tracking, utilizing zero-shot and few-shot learning to enhance interaction capabilities. Lastly, Table Understanding involves interpreting structured data, with advancements in zero-shot and few-shot learning, as well as parameter tuning methods, to improve model performance in handling tabular data. The text references various studies and frameworks that contribute to these advancements in NLP.

This section discusses the application of Large Language Models (LLMs) in various Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks, including Summarization, Code Generation, Machine Translation, and Mathematical Reasoning. In Summarization, LLMs like GPT-3 excel in zero-shot learning, producing concise summaries without fine-tuning, while few-shot learning techniques enhance summary quality through in-context learning. Parameter-tuning methods, including full-parameter and parameter-efficient tuning, optimize LLMs for specific summarization tasks. In Code Generation, LLMs demonstrate strong zero-shot and few-shot learning capabilities, with models like CodeT5+ and CodeGemma leading advancements. Full-parameter tuning and reinforcement learning strategies further enhance code generation performance. For Machine Translation, LLMs improve translation accuracy through zero-shot and few-shot learning, with parameter-tuning methods refining their capabilities. Lastly, in Mathematical Reasoning, LLMs utilize zero-shot and few-shot learning to tackle complex problems, with parameter-tuning techniques enhancing their reasoning abilities. Overall, LLMs present a unified generative solution for diverse NLP tasks, though they still lag behind smaller supervised models, indicating the need for ongoing fine-tuning to achieve substantial improvements.

The section discusses future directions for advancements in large language models (LLMs) in natural language processing (NLP). Key areas include enhancing multilingual LLMs to support over 7,000 languages, improving multi-modal LLMs for complex reasoning, and optimizing tool usage for practical applications. Challenges in these areas involve enhancing performance in low-resource languages, effective multi-modal interaction, and efficient tool planning. Additionally, the text addresses the need for advanced logical reasoning through X-of-thought (XoT) techniques, managing hallucinations in LLM outputs, ensuring safety in applications, and developing Long Chain-of-Thought (Long-CoT) methods for deeper reasoning. Each area presents specific challenges, such as universal step decomposition, safety benchmark construction, and adaptive reasoning length control, which are critical for the future development of LLMs in NLP tasks.

The conclusion of this work provides a comprehensive overview of large language models (LLMs) in natural language processing (NLP), introducing a unified taxonomy that differentiates between parameter-frozen and parameter-tuning paradigms. It highlights emerging research frontiers and challenges, aiming to guide future studies while maintaining a publicly accessible resource website for ongoing developments. Supported by grants from the National Natural Science Foundation of China and utilizing resources from the High-Performance Computing Center of Central South University, the authors intend for this work to offer valuable insights for the effective development of LLMs. The research encompasses various papers and preprints that explore advancements in LLM applications across diverse tasks, including task-oriented dialogue, summarization, machine translation, and multimodal reasoning. Notable contributions include innovative models and techniques such as "Diaggpt," "Cabinet," TableGPT, and Codet5, as well as studies on dialogue state tracking, iterative summarization, and video reasoning. The collective efforts reflect ongoing research trends and innovations in the field, showcasing the collaborative nature of AI research across institutions.
